# Eonrise brief

**Question:** how can a system retrieve analogous solutions to a problem from distant research fields

**Root topic:** retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields

**Status:** partial — no additional distinct queries

**Evidence:** 50 papers kept of 52 retrieved (34 on topic), 77 concepts

## Grounded map

- **Mechanism:** cross domain retrieval, relational retrieval, mechanism skeleton
- **Measurement:** not grounded yet
- **Failure Mode:** machine learning similarity metrics, far field retrieval skill, far analogies zero shot
- **Method:** not grounded yet
- **Neighbor Field:** engineering design, information retrieval, human computer interaction

## Stated limitations

- **machine learning similarity metrics** — "Stated motivation: hand-created databases do not scale, and machine-learning similarity metrics struggle to account for structural similarity, which is central to analogy."
- **far field retrieval skill** — "Related work notes novice designers lacking far-field retrieval skill are constrained to patents with surface similarities, and retrieving domain-similar patents led to ideas that "
- **far analogies zero shot** — "Stated limitation: while LLMs largely recognize near analogies, even the largest struggle with far analogies zero-shot, with GPT-4 scoring below random"

## Same shape, other fields

- **Forecasting the future of artificial intelligence with machine learning-based link prediction in an exponentially growing knowledge network** (2023, Machine Learning) — shares machine learning similarity metrics

## Concept directions

- **down:** cross domain retrieval
- **sideways:** analogical search, analogical retrieval, analogical transfer, scientific creativity

**Gaps:** measurement, method

**Not in this literature:** measurement, method — two full rounds produced no candidate at all, so the run stopped spending queries on it rather than calling it an unfilled gap.

- `analogical search metric`

corpus_papers.abstract: Distills each paper into a domain- and method-name-stripped faceted computational fingerprint (free-text mechanism skeleton plus controlled facets) to find cross-field pairs solving the same problem, e.g. Kalman filter, Bayesian forecasting and data assimilation. On 109 papers in 18 method families, the skeleton raises cross-domain retrieval average precision over the abstract from 0.222 to 0.513 (whole fingerprint 0.557), showing raw abstracts retrieve poorly across fields.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Same Problem, Different Field: Cross-Domain Solution Import via Domain-Stripped Computational Fingerprints

corpus_papers.abstract: Explores learning simpler structural representations called problem schemas, which specify the purpose of solutions, to find analogies in large idea repositories such as patents. Stated motivation: hand-created databases do not scale, and machine-learning similarity metrics struggle to account for structural similarity, which is central to analogy.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Accelerating Innovation Through Analogy Mining

corpus_papers.abstract: Transforms a design problem into a functional representation and searches patent databases using a mapped functional basis to find near- and far-field analogies for ideation. Uses a vector space model to score functional similarity between design problems and patent descriptions; the case study shows analogies ranging from literal near-field to far-field cross-domain solutions.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Function Based Design-by-Analogy: A Functional Vector Approach to Analogical Search

corpus_papers.abstract: Shows comparing two analogous examples facilitates deriving a schema that supports transfer to a structurally similar problem. Reported effect: 45% of participants in the comparison condition spontaneously generated the convergence solution to the tumor problem versus 21% in the single-analog condition.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Schema induction and analogical transfer

corpus_papers.abstract: Automatically generates abstract representations of source-domain content and applies them to discover analogous objects in semantically distant target domains. It can find deep functional analogies even where there is a misleading superficial matching of terms between query and target domains.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Method for retrieving semantically distant analogies (US 6,523,026 B1)

corpus_papers.abstract: Simplifies analogical relations to purpose (what problem does it solve) and mechanism (how); SOLVENT is a mixed-initiative system where humans annotate background, purpose, mechanism and findings of papers and a model builds a semantic representation to find cross-domain analogies. It finds more analogies than baseline IR approaches and results are useful to experts. Depends on human annotation.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Augmenting Scientific Creativity with an Analogical Search Engine

corpus_papers.abstract: Presents a representation that automatically breaks products into fine-grained functional aspects capturing the purposes and mechanisms of ideas, built from large repositories of products, patents and scientific papers. Used to support functional search for ideas and exploration of the design space around a focal problem.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Scaling Creative Inspiration with Fine-Grained Functional Aspects of Ideas

corpus_papers.abstract: Exploratory search system where users select a portion of text core to their interest from a paper abstract and retrieve papers highly similar to that aspect but differing in domain. Motivation: improved scholarly search helps in familiar domains but may fall short of helping scientists explore diverse ideas outside them.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Augmenting Scientific Creativity with Retrieval across Knowledge Domains
corpus_papers.venue: NAACL 2022 Workshop on Bridging HCI and NLP

corpus_papers.abstract: Cognitive engineering design study of how analogical distance of stimuli affects generated solutions, using the U.S. patent database as repository. Near and far stimuli were chosen from patent structure built with latent semantic analysis and a Bayesian algorithm for discovering structural form.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: The Meaning of Near and Far: The Impact of Structuring Design Databases and the Effect of Distance of Analogy on Design Output

corpus_papers.abstract: Studies retrieval of biology articles for engineering design problems. Stated limitation: in situ studies of biologically inspired design retrieval identified findability and recognizability of relevant biology articles on the Web as major challenges.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Biological Solutions for Engineering Problems: A Study in Cross-Domain Textual Case-Based Reasoning

corpus_papers.abstract: Both structural features, which play a causal role in determining possible solutions, and salient surface features, which do not, influence spontaneous selection of an analogue. Structural features have greater impact on the ability to use an analogue once its relevance is pointed out; spontaneous retrieval remains influenced by surface features.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Surface and structural similarity in analogical transfer

corpus_papers.abstract: The thesaurus acts as a set of correspondent terms to the functions and flows of the functional basis, providing term mapping between engineering and biological domains for engineers with limited biological background. It increases retrieval of relevant biological information, with a reported 33% improvement in relevant solutions for specific functions like detection.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: An Engineering-to-Biology Thesaurus for Engineering Design
topic_path: function vocabulary bridging between engineering and biology

corpus_papers.abstract: Provides biologically meaningful keywords for the functional terms of the engineering Functional Basis so that engineers can search biological text for solutions to a functional need. The keyword set supports bio-inspired concept generation from function statements.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Biologically Meaningful Keywords for Functional Terms of the Functional Basis

corpus_papers.abstract: AskNature.org is a biomimetic database that includes a Biomimicry Taxonomy, biological strategy pages organized by function, search and tri-browse features, and bio-inspired product pages as examples of design successes.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: The AskNature Database: Enabling Solutions in Biomimetic Design

corpus_papers.abstract: LLMs in a Pinterest-like interface support identifying key solution mechanisms, transferring them to the problem domain and considering tradeoffs, using a tree-of-life approach for diverse inspirations. Users generated more ideas, rated higher in creative quality and more diverse. Limitation: BioSpark was limited in conveying active ingredients, the core abstraction underpinning how mechanisms work, and generative hallucination is a concern.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: BioSpark: Beyond Analogical Inspiration to LLM-augmented Transfer

corpus_papers.abstract: Re-presents a problem in terms of its abstract structure and lets people use this structural representation to find analogies; a crowdsourcing process helps people navigate a large dataset. Crowds find the most useful inspirations when the problem domain is represented abstractly and constraints more concretely.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Searching for analogical ideas with crowds

corpus_papers.abstract: Aims to provide evidence on the effect of analogical distance on ideation; the effect on design outcomes is controversial. Designers not trained in design-by-analogy benefit from sources sharing sub-functions and context with the target, producing ideas of higher novelty and quality than those exposed to more distant analogies.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Testing ideation performance on a large set of designers: effects of analogical distance
topic_path: near analogies can beat far for untrained designers
corpus_papers.venue: Int. J. Design Creativity and Innovation

corpus_papers.abstract: Notes that automatically extracting analogical knowledge and constructing semantic relations between knowledge levels is a key problem for design-by-analogy; a knowledge graph mines semantic relationships between levels to enable structured retrieval.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Knowledge graph-assisted design-by-analogy: promoting product innovation through structured analogical knowledge retrieval

corpus_papers.abstract: Applies non-negative matrix factorization iteratively to build hierarchical repositories of design solutions from patents processed into component-, behavior- or material-based content, so designers can explore clusters of analogical stimuli.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Design-by-Analogy: Exploring for Analogical Inspiration With Behavior, Material, and Component-Based Structural Representation of Patent Databases

corpus_papers.abstract: Conceptual model of knowledge transfer for cross-industry innovation, where novel ideas emerge from combining distant knowledge and interaction with idea suppliers from distant domains.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Knowledge Transition: A Conceptual Model of Knowledge Transfer for Cross-Industry Innovation
corpus_papers.venue: Int. J. Innovation and Technology Management

corpus_papers.abstract: Argues diverse and novel recommendations in paper recommendation expose researchers to ideas from other fields, removing barriers to interdisciplinary research; assesses disciplinary diversity of recommended papers.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Facilitating Interdisciplinary Knowledge Transfer with Research Paper Recommender Systems

corpus_papers.abstract: Studies spontaneous word choice for objects in five application-related domains and finds surprisingly large variability: two people favor the same term with probability less than 0.20. Limitation stated: using one designer's favorite single word results in 80-90 percent failure rates in many common situations. Derives an optimal 'unlimited aliasing' strategy shown to give several-fold improvements; three access terms improve success by 50-100% over a single term.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: The vocabulary problem in human-system communication

corpus_papers.abstract: Builds EntityQuestions from Wikidata facts and finds dense retrievers drastically underperform sparse methods. Limitation: dense retrievers only generalize to common entities unless the question pattern was seen in training; data augmentation does not fix the generalization problem. Argues a more robust passage encoder helps.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
corpus_papers.title: Simple Entity-Centric Questions Challenge Dense Retrievers
topic_path: dense retrieval failure on rare terms

corpus_papers.abstract: Humans annotate aspects of research papers (background, purpose, mechanism, findings) and a computational model builds a semantic representation from these annotations to find analogies among papers. Finds more analogies than baseline information-retrieval approaches, annotations generalize beyond domain, and found analogies are useful to experts.
corpus_papers.title: SOLVENT: A Mixed Initiative System for Finding Analogies between Research Papers

corpus_papers.abstract: Analogical search engine for scientists that finds structurally similar problems across knowledge domains; explores distributing analogy, finding deep structural patterns across domains, over many information processors.
corpus_papers.title: Augmenting Scientific Creativity with an Analogical Search Engine

corpus_papers.abstract: Patent-based search tool for concept generation that maps functions using a functional patent vocabulary (about 2,100 functions extracted from 65,000 patents). Related work notes novice designers lacking far-field retrieval skill are constrained to patents with surface similarities, and retrieving domain-similar patents led to ideas that directly copied the patent designs.
corpus_papers.title: Patent-based analogy search tool for innovative concept generation

corpus_papers.abstract: Operationalizes theories of analogy with surface and system mappings to build a benchmark covering far (cross-domain) and near (within-domain) analogies and disanalogies. Stated limitation: while LLMs largely recognize near analogies, even the largest struggle with far analogies zero-shot, with GPT-4 scoring below random; solved examples and chain-of-thought help.
corpus_papers.title: ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews evaluation of LBD systems: domain-expert vetting, discovery replication and time-slicing. Replication is cheap but systems are usually tested only against a small set of confirmed discoveries, often Swanson's own. Time-slicing treats co-occurrences appearing after a cutoff year as gold discoveries; however, using co-occurrences as a proxy for discoveries is a dramatic simplification, with very few co-occurrences representing a true discovery and the vast majority being meaningless or poorly informative.
corpus_papers.title: Literature-based discovery: addressing the issue of the subpar evaluation methodology

corpus_papers.abstract: Surveys data-driven design-by-analogy studies and categorizes them by data, methods and applications into four categories: analogy encoding, retrieval, mapping, and evaluation. Benchmarks the field against frontier data science and AI research to identify opportunities.
corpus_papers.title: Data-Driven Design-By-Analogy: State-of-the-Art and Future Directions

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews function-based patent search, a TRIZ-inspired direction that theorizes invention from patent observation. Patents can help designers find technologies providing desired functionality, find applications of specific structures, and resolve engineering conflicts; the title flags open problems remaining.
corpus_papers.title: Function-based patent search: achievements and open problems

corpus_papers.abstract: Biologically inspired design invents technology by analogy to biological systems. Describes semantic tagging of biology articles using Structure-Behavior-Function models, and an engineering-to-biology thesaurus that maps functional-basis terms to biological terms to make biology accessible to engineers with limited biological knowledge.
corpus_papers.title: A computational approach to biologically inspired design

corpus_papers.abstract: Model reconciling that structure outweighs surface in similarity judgments of items in working memory, yet in retrieval superficial similarity is more important than structural similarity, while purely structural remindings sometimes occur. Uses a two-stage process: a computationally cheap non-structural matcher filters long-term memory, then structural alignment (SME) selects among candidates.
corpus_papers.title: MAC/FAC: A Model of Similarity-Based Retrieval

corpus_papers.abstract: Addresses inert knowledge, past cases that cannot be spontaneously retrieved when relevant. Analogical abstraction, i.e. comparing and abstracting across cases, supports relational retrieval of past events. Retrieval otherwise tends to be driven by surface similarity such as similar characters and settings.
corpus_papers.title: Reviving Inert Knowledge: Analogical Abstraction Supports Relational Retrieval of Past Events

corpus_papers.abstract: Compares three ways to find bio-inspiration: the AskNature database, a natural language processing approach over a large corpus of biological publications, and consultation of an expert biologist. The NLP approach retrieves relevant publications with good recall without an expert; however, extracting the working principles from the retrieved biological articles is error-prone and time consuming.
corpus_papers.title: Where and how to find bio-inspiration? A comparison of search approaches for bio-inspired design
corpus_papers.venue: CIRP Journal of Manufacturing Science and Technology

corpus_papers.abstract: Uses retrieval-augmented generation, merging semantic retrieval with generative reasoning, to translate biological knowledge for stages of biomimicry design and mitigate hallucinations in LLM outputs.
corpus_papers.title: An Innovative Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Stage-Specific Knowledge Translation in Biomimicry Design

corpus_papers.abstract: Perspective on moving analogy out of one person's mind and distributing it across human and machine processors. Aims to overcome cognitive fixation, scale to large idea repositories and support problems with multiple constraints; reports first steps with crowds and AI and names core challenges still critical to realizing the vision.
corpus_papers.title: Scaling up analogical innovation with crowds and AI
topic_path: crowd and AI analogy at scale

corpus_papers.abstract: Examines how analogical distance (near vs far), commonness and modality of examples affect ideation. Stated limitation: 'Drawing inspiration from examples by analogy can be a powerful tool for innovative design during conceptual ideation but also carries the risk of negative design outcomes (e.g., design fixation), depending on key properties of examples.'
corpus_papers.title: On the Benefits and Pitfalls of Analogies for Innovative Design: Ideation Performance Based on Analogical Distance, Commonness, and Modality of Examples

corpus_papers.abstract: Analyses bio-inspired products in AskNature to categorise analogical transfer. In 71% of the products multiple categories of analogical transfer were present, so transfer is complex, and the majority of commercialised bio-inspired products did not rely on physical characteristic-based analogies alone.
corpus_papers.title: Establishing Analogy Categories for Bio-Inspired Design

corpus_papers.abstract: A divergent thinking tool built on bio-inspired design knowledge from AskNature, aimed at the difficulty designers face extracting design knowledge from biological information; keyword-centric search and fragmented knowledge frameworks may hamper efficiency.
corpus_papers.title: AskNatureNet: A divergent thinking tool based on bio-inspired design knowledge

corpus_papers.abstract: Benchmark of 24 tasks across classification, regression, ranking and search formats. Limitation stated: state-of-the-art models like SPECTER and SciNCL struggle to generalize across task formats, and simple multi-task training fails to improve them. Learning multiple embeddings per document tailored to each format (SPECTER2) improves performance by over 2 points absolute.
corpus_papers.title: SciRepEval: A Multi-Format Benchmark for Scientific Document Representations

corpus_papers.abstract: A general method for functionally representing biological systems uses functional representation and abstraction techniques to translate biological systems into an engineering context. The method takes the essential function the design must fulfill as input.
corpus_papers.title: Function-based, biologically inspired concept generation

corpus_papers.abstract: In vivo study of analogy use in engineering design teams. Concepts were more similar to their preceding concepts after far analogy use compared to baseline, yet far analogies increased the team's concept generation rate.
corpus_papers.title: The Impact of Analogies on Creative Concept Generation: Lessons From an In Vivo Study in Engineering Design

corpus_papers.abstract: Systematic review that concludes filter bubbles exist in recommender systems, examining forms of bias that contribute to personalization problems arising in system design, implementation, evaluation, and user interaction.
corpus_papers.title: Filter Bubbles in Recommender Systems: Fact or Fallacy - A Systematic Review

corpus_papers.abstract: Proposes a framework for transferring technologies between industries as cross-industry innovation.
corpus_papers.title: A Framework for Cross-Industry Innovation: Transferring Technologies between Industries
corpus_papers.venue: Int. J. Innovation and Technology Management

corpus_papers.abstract: Simulates Swanson's discoveries: two disjoint literature sets that do not cite or co-cite each other are linked through intermediate terms such as blood viscosity, platelet aggregation and vascular reactivity, a link later verified in clinical trials.
corpus_papers.title: Using concepts in literature-based discovery: Simulating Swanson's Raynaud-fish oil and migraine-magnesium discoveries

corpus_papers.abstract: Survey of LBD under the ABC model, in which A-B is known in one area and B-C in another and an A-C relationship is proposed. Notes that most approaches rely on PubMed and often only article abstracts, omitting contextual relationships valuable for complex hypothesis generation.
corpus_papers.title: Recent Advances and Future Directions in Literature-Based Discovery

corpus_papers.abstract: Formulates hypothesis generation as link prediction over a temporally evolving knowledge graph, using active curriculum learning; temporal interactions between entities inform prediction of future relationships.
corpus_papers.title: Link prediction for hypothesis generation: an active curriculum learning infused temporal graph-based approach

corpus_papers.abstract: Predicts future links in a knowledge network of AI concepts (Science4Cast) so as to suggest concept pairs that will be studied jointly.
corpus_papers.title: Forecasting the future of artificial intelligence with machine learning-based link prediction in an exponentially growing knowledge network

corpus_papers.abstract: Frames creative information exploration as finding new, surprising, valuable relationships that conventional retrieval and data mining would not reveal, via bisociation: perceiving a situation in two unrelated matrices of thought.
corpus_papers.title: Towards Creative Information Exploration Based on Koestler's Concept of Bisociation

corpus_papers.abstract: Survey of hypothesis generation and validation. LLMs are often constrained by reliance on established knowledge bases and historical data, which can limit transformative or genuinely novel hypotheses and restricts exploration of counterintuitive or uncharted areas.
corpus_papers.title: Scientific Hypothesis Generation and Validation: Methods, Datasets, and Future Directions

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews Swanson's literature-based discovery: connecting literatures that are logically related but bibliographically noninteractive, exemplified by magnesium deprivation and migraine, two literatures never jointly cited that yielded a hypothesis later supported by clinical trials.
corpus_papers.title: Undiscovered Public Knowledge: a Ten-Year Update

corpus_papers.abstract: Uses LLM agents for ontology matching, evaluated on OAEI tracks; matches ontologies whose concept labels differ in wording, a form of cross-vocabulary alignment.
corpus_papers.title: Agent-OM: Leveraging LLM Agents for Ontology Matching

papers.abstract: Automatically generates abstract representations of source-domain content and applies them to discover analogous objects in semantically distant target domains. It can find deep functional analogies even where there is a misleading superficial matching of terms between query and target domains.

papers.title: Method for retrieving semantically distant analogies (US 6,523,026 B1)

papers.abstract: Both structural features, which play a causal role in determining possible solutions, and salient surface features, which do not, influence spontaneous selection of an analogue. Structural features have greater impact on the ability to use an analogue once its relevance is pointed out; spontaneous retrieval remains influenced by surface features.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: Surface and structural similarity in analogical transfer

papers.abstract: The thesaurus acts as a set of correspondent terms to the functions and flows of the functional basis, providing term mapping between engineering and biological domains for engineers with limited biological background. It increases retrieval of relevant biological information, with a reported 33% improvement in relevant solutions for specific functions like detection.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: An Engineering-to-Biology Thesaurus for Engineering Design
topic_path: function vocabulary bridging between engineering and biology

papers.abstract: Notes that automatically extracting analogical knowledge and constructing semantic relations between knowledge levels is a key problem for design-by-analogy; a knowledge graph mines semantic relationships between levels to enable structured retrieval.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: Knowledge graph-assisted design-by-analogy: promoting product innovation through structured analogical knowledge retrieval

papers.abstract: Studies spontaneous word choice for objects in five application-related domains and finds surprisingly large variability: two people favor the same term with probability less than 0.20. Limitation stated: using one designer's favorite single word results in 80-90 percent failure rates in many common situations. Derives an optimal 'unlimited aliasing' strategy shown to give several-fold improvements; three access terms improve success by 50-100% over a single term.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: The vocabulary problem in human-system communication

papers.abstract: Patent-based search tool for concept generation that maps functions using a functional patent vocabulary (about 2,100 functions extracted from 65,000 patents). Related work notes novice designers lacking far-field retrieval skill are constrained to patents with surface similarities, and retrieving domain-similar patents led to ideas that directly copied the patent designs.
papers.title: Patent-based analogy search tool for innovative concept generation

papers.abstract: Biologically inspired design invents technology by analogy to biological systems. Describes semantic tagging of biology articles using Structure-Behavior-Function models, and an engineering-to-biology thesaurus that maps functional-basis terms to biological terms to make biology accessible to engineers with limited biological knowledge.
papers.title: A computational approach to biologically inspired design

papers.abstract: Model reconciling that structure outweighs surface in similarity judgments of items in working memory, yet in retrieval superficial similarity is more important than structural similarity, while purely structural remindings sometimes occur. Uses a two-stage process: a computationally cheap non-structural matcher filters long-term memory, then structural alignment (SME) selects among candidates.
papers.title: MAC/FAC: A Model of Similarity-Based Retrieval

papers.abstract: Addresses inert knowledge, past cases that cannot be spontaneously retrieved when relevant. Analogical abstraction, i.e. comparing and abstracting across cases, supports relational retrieval of past events. Retrieval otherwise tends to be driven by surface similarity such as similar characters and settings.
papers.title: Reviving Inert Knowledge: Analogical Abstraction Supports Relational Retrieval of Past Events

papers.abstract: A general method for functionally representing biological systems uses functional representation and abstraction techniques to translate biological systems into an engineering context. The method takes the essential function the design must fulfill as input.
papers.title: Function-based, biologically inspired concept generation

papers.abstract: LLMs in a Pinterest-like interface support identifying key solution mechanisms, transferring them to the problem domain and considering tradeoffs, using a tree-of-life approach for diverse inspirations. Users generated more ideas, rated higher in creative quality and more diverse. Limitation: BioSpark was limited in conveying active ingredients, the core abstraction underpinning how mechanisms work, and generative hallucination is a concern.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: BioSpark: Beyond Analogical Inspiration to LLM-augmented Transfer

papers.abstract: Uses retrieval-augmented generation, merging semantic retrieval with generative reasoning, to translate biological knowledge for stages of biomimicry design and mitigate hallucinations in LLM outputs.
papers.title: An Innovative Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Stage-Specific Knowledge Translation in Biomimicry Design

papers.abstract: Survey of LBD under the ABC model, in which A-B is known in one area and B-C in another and an A-C relationship is proposed. Notes that most approaches rely on PubMed and often only article abstracts, omitting contextual relationships valuable for complex hypothesis generation.
papers.title: Recent Advances and Future Directions in Literature-Based Discovery

papers.abstract: Survey of hypothesis generation and validation. LLMs are often constrained by reliance on established knowledge bases and historical data, which can limit transformative or genuinely novel hypotheses and restricts exploration of counterintuitive or uncharted areas.
papers.title: Scientific Hypothesis Generation and Validation: Methods, Datasets, and Future Directions

papers.abstract: Formulates hypothesis generation as link prediction over a temporally evolving knowledge graph, using active curriculum learning; temporal interactions between entities inform prediction of future relationships.
papers.title: Link prediction for hypothesis generation: an active curriculum learning infused temporal graph-based approach

papers.abstract: Argues diverse and novel recommendations in paper recommendation expose researchers to ideas from other fields, removing barriers to interdisciplinary research; assesses disciplinary diversity of recommended papers.
found_by: retrieve analogous solutions problem distant fields
papers.title: Facilitating Interdisciplinary Knowledge Transfer with Research Paper Recommender Systems

papers.abstract: Reviews evaluation of LBD systems: domain-expert vetting, discovery replication and time-slicing. Replication is cheap but systems are usually tested only against a small set of confirmed discoveries, often Swanson's own. Time-slicing treats co-occurrences appearing after a cutoff year as gold discoveries; however, using co-occurrences as a proxy for discoveries is a dramatic simplification, with very few co-occurrences representing a true discovery and the vast majority being meaningless or poorly informative.
papers.title: Literature-based discovery: addressing the issue of the subpar evaluation methodology

papers.abstract: Systematic review that concludes filter bubbles exist in recommender systems, examining forms of bias that contribute to personalization problems arising in system design, implementation, evaluation, and user interaction.
papers.title: Filter Bubbles in Recommender Systems: Fact or Fallacy - A Systematic Review

papers.abstract: Predicts future links in a knowledge network of AI concepts (Science4Cast) so as to suggest concept pairs that will be studied jointly.
papers.title: Forecasting the future of artificial intelligence with machine learning-based link prediction in an exponentially growing knowledge network

papers.abstract: Uses LLM agents for ontology matching, evaluated on OAEI tracks; matches ontologies whose concept labels differ in wording, a form of cross-vocabulary alignment.
papers.title: Agent-OM: Leveraging LLM Agents for Ontology Matching

papers.abstract: Benchmark of 24 tasks across classification, regression, ranking and search formats. Limitation stated: state-of-the-art models like SPECTER and SciNCL struggle to generalize across task formats, and simple multi-task training fails to improve them. Learning multiple embeddings per document tailored to each format (SPECTER2) improves performance by over 2 points absolute.
papers.title: SciRepEval: A Multi-Format Benchmark for Scientific Document Representations

papers.abstract: Builds EntityQuestions from Wikidata facts and finds dense retrievers drastically underperform sparse methods. Limitation: dense retrievers only generalize to common entities unless the question pattern was seen in training; data augmentation does not fix the generalization problem. Argues a more robust passage encoder helps.

papers.title: Simple Entity-Centric Questions Challenge Dense Retrievers

papers.abstract: Proposes a framework for transferring technologies between industries as cross-industry innovation.
papers.title: A Framework for Cross-Industry Innovation: Transferring Technologies between Industries
papers.venue: Int. J. Innovation and Technology Management

papers.abstract: Perspective on moving analogy out of one person's mind and distributing it across human and machine processors. Aims to overcome cognitive fixation, scale to large idea repositories and support problems with multiple constraints; reports first steps with crowds and AI and names core challenges still critical to realizing the vision.
papers.title: Scaling up analogical innovation with crowds and AI
topic_path: crowd and AI analogy at scale

papers.abstract: Conceptual model of knowledge transfer for cross-industry innovation, where novel ideas emerge from combining distant knowledge and interaction with idea suppliers from distant domains.

papers.title: Knowledge Transition: A Conceptual Model of Knowledge Transfer for Cross-Industry Innovation
papers.venue: Int. J. Innovation and Technology Management

papers.abstract: Frames creative information exploration as finding new, surprising, valuable relationships that conventional retrieval and data mining would not reveal, via bisociation: perceiving a situation in two unrelated matrices of thought.
papers.title: Towards Creative Information Exploration Based on Koestler's Concept of Bisociation
